title: Defender for Cloud Recommendations

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `mscs:azure:defender` events with `recommendationState="Active"` into `index=azure`. Confirm UC-4.2.43 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `mscs:azure:defender` traffic without `recommendationState="Active"`. Confirm UC-4.2.43 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=azure` sourcetype=`mscs:azure:defender` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, Defender export API; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:defender" recommendationState="Active"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.43_defender_for_cloud_recom_43"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.2.43 — Defender for Cloud Recommendations: queries Microsoft Azure `mscs:azure:defender` for search criteria `recommendationState="Active"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On Microsoft Azure, detecting 'Defender for Cloud Recommendations' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.2.43 drives medium-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Export recommendations on schedule via Logic App or Microsoft Graph security API to Splunk. Track mean time to remediate by severity. Executive dashboard of secure score trend if ingested.
visualization: Bar chart (recommendations by type), Table (severity, count), Line chart (open recommendations over time).
knownFalsePositives: A fresh scanner run or a vendor re-rate can resurface a finding we already know about. We deduplicate on resource and time and we only escalate when the exposure is new or the severity stepped up.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, Defender export API with the modular input for `mscs:azure:defender`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Export recommendations on schedule via Logic App or Microsoft Graph security API to Splunk. Track mean time to remediate by severity. Executive dashboard of secure score trend if ingested.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:defender" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:defender" recommendationState="Active"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.43_defender_for_cloud_recom_43"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `mscs:azure:defender` in `index=azure` to detect defender for cloud recommendations. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_43_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Bar chart (recommendations by type), Table (severity, count), Line chart (open recommendations over time)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, Defender export API and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of defender for cloud recommendations so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
